hooks.text: 300 skeletons proved that everyone in Herculaneum didn't escape the volcano.
Three hundred skeletons were found huddled inside vaulted shoreline boat houses.
The people of Herculaneum were trapped by a rising tide and a raging sea.

title: Why Did Everyone Think Herculaneum Escaped Vesuvius? 😳
description: For centuries, historians believed the Roman town of Herculaneum escaped the eruption of Mount Vesuvius until archaeologists found hundreds of skeletons in the shoreline boathouses.

beats.text: 300 skeletons proved that everyone in Herculaneum didn't escape the volcano.
beats.visual: painting of the eruption of Mount Vesuvius by Pierre-Jacques Volaire, 1777

beats.text: That comforting narrative shattered when archaeologists excavated the ancient shoreline.
beats.visual: photograph of Herculaneum ancient beach and boathouses, 2020

beats.text: Victims waited inside vaulted stone boathouses for rescue boats that never arrived.
beats.visual: photograph of Herculaneum ruins fornici waterfront, 2018

beats.text: A superheated pyroclastic surge rushed down the mountain.
beats.visual: painting of the eruption of Mount Vesuvius by William Turner, 1817

beats.text: Extreme thermal shock caused instant death for everyone by the shore.
beats.visual: photograph of Herculaneum ancient ruins and shore, 2021

beats.text: For centuries, the world believed they had all gotten away.
beats.visual: painting of the eruption of Mount Vesuvius by Johann Christian Dahl, 1824

better_than_last: This episode applies the myth_vs_fact structure with reviewer adjustments to challenge a common historical assumption using archaeological evidence in under 30 seconds.
